quotes.text: Add an optional review page or run validations after a user enters their payment details.
If you intend to specify `setup_future_usage`, don’t set `payment_method_save_usage` in the same payment transaction because `setup_future_usage` controls the save behavior.
If your integration renders the Payment Element before creating an Intent, we suppress microdeposit verification for US bank accounts when the payment amount is 0.
Use [stripe.confirmPayment](https://docs.stripe.com/js/payment_intents/confirm_payment) to complete the payment using details from the Payment Element.

findings: Semantic raw delta: the two-step review/validation/tax purpose and deferred Payment Element → client ConfirmationToken → server PaymentIntent → client confirmPayment path remain in both captures (new raw lines 5-13, 404-410, 653-661, 743-751; old raw lines 4-12, 401-407, 655-663, 763-771). November adds specific zero-amount US-bank microdeposit suppression and renames an Elements option in its table (new raw lines 382, 397-403; old raw lines 374-399; diff lines 423-464).

November's server setup and PaymentIntent examples switch Node.js to Ruby, the Stripe.js script example moves dahlia to endive, and image URLs/code style change (new raw lines 15-30, 55-69, 263-323, 665-741; old raw lines 14-25, 49-63, 260-320, 667-761; diff lines 3-20, 40-85, 254-363, 709-873). These are captured example/version/presentation changes, not proof of API deprecation or payment success.

Existing-summary baseline accuracy: source lines 13-22 conveys the core review flow but omits elements.submit before ConfirmationToken (new raw lines 437-465; old raw lines 434-462), overstates that all Elements options must match PI parameters exactly (source line 26 versus conditional match warning and table in new raw lines 376-402), and presents tax linking as a fixed step although the guide calls tax optional and its PI hook is commented (new raw lines 591-600, 663-699; old raw lines 594-604, 665-706).

Current source lines 31-34 says no ACSS direct debits, while both captures specify pre-authorized ACSS debits; they also condition customer_balance on a client-created deferred Intent with dynamic payment methods and require a server-created PaymentIntent with Account or Customer and returned client_secret for that route (new raw lines 33-39; old raw lines 27-33).

Root wiki/index.md line 7 routes through wiki/stripe-index.md lines 555 and 729 to wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-intents.md lines 43-48 and 145-148 and mapped source; source lines 1-9 lacks canonical_url and source lines 45-47 only link the May raw, so provenance and November route need correction.

source_assessments.reason: The November capture adds scoped behavior and an option name, while the mapped source has baseline overstatements and missing provenance. A dated dual-raw source correction is needed; no source edit is authorized in this review-only handoff.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/build-a-two-step-confirmation, the November guide documents an optional review, validation or tax step after Payment Element entry: configure web Elements, submit details, create a ConfirmationToken, inspect payment_method_preview on the server, optionally calculate tax, then create a server PaymentIntent and pass its client secret to client-side stripe.confirmPayment with the token and return_url (new raw lines 5-13, 404-410, 437-465, 541-661, 743-751). The May guide describes the same central flow (old raw lines 4-12, 401-407, 542-663, 763-771). Enabled payment methods, live HTTPS and direct Stripe.js loading matter; BLIK and ACSS pre-authorized debits are excluded, and client-created deferred Intents cannot use customer_balance with dynamic methods unless the PaymentIntent is instead server-created with Account or Customer (new raw lines 33-55). Saved-method CustomerSession uses a Customer or customer-configured Account, the latter GA for Connect and preview for others with preview version (new raw lines 249-261). source-stripe-two-step-confirmation.md captures the outline but omits submit, broadens some conditions, and misses November raw provenance (current source lines 1-9, 13-34, 45-47). Token creation, review display, Intent creation and browser return do not establish payment success or settlement.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/build-a-two-step-confirmation, the substantive November differences are the scoped zero-amount US-bank microdeposit suppression, Elements table's allowedPaymentMethodTypes in place of paymentMethodTypes, revised save-behavior explanation, and Accounts v2 preview enrollment route (new raw lines 253-261, 376-403; old raw lines 250-258, 374-399). Ruby replacing Node.js server examples, endive replacing dahlia in the Stripe.js script example, images and code formatting are presentation/version evidence, not proof of deprecation or mandatory SDK migration (new raw lines 21-30, 55-61, 665-741; old raw lines 20-25, 49-55, 667-761). source-stripe-two-step-confirmation.md should retain May provenance, add November raw and canonical_url, qualify optional tax and exact ACSS wording, and narrow its Elements matching claim (current source lines 1-9, 21-34, 45-47). May warned a combined setup_future_usage/payment_method_save_usage transaction caused an integration error whereas November says setup_future_usage controls save behavior; both say not to combine them, so preserve dates and flag the explanation conflict (old raw line 250; new raw line 253). Account versus Customer and Connect GA versus preview, client versus server confirmation, return_url handling, and PaymentIntent state must remain distinct; neither capture proves payment success, eligibility or funds availability (new raw lines 255-261, 653-661, 743-751).
